title: How to Pay in China as a Tourist in 2026 (Do This First) | China Travel Expert
description:
Worried that "cashless China" will leave you stuck at the counter? Here's exactly how a foreign tourist pays in China in 2026 — in the order that actually works.

The big change: you can now use Alipay and WeChat Pay WITHOUT a Chinese bank account — register with your passport and phone, link an international Visa, Mastercard or JCB, and verify with a passport photo and a live face scan. That one setup covers roughly 90% of what you'll pay for. Your physical foreign card still helps at high-end hotels and big shops, but not at small local places or on buses. Watch the in-app foreign-card limit (reported around ¥3,000–6,500 / about $400–900 per transaction in 2026, raised under the central bank's directives). And carry a little cash — renminbi is still legal tender and ATMs at Bank of China and ICBC are the most foreign-card-friendly. This is a practical guide; opinions on ordering are mine, and the rules and prices are verified for September 2026.

🧭 Expert Tip: Install BOTH apps and finish verification at home on your own wifi, days before you fly — never jet-lagged in the arrivals hall on a foreign SIM.
